releases.notes: Operational visibility and multi-site polish. The admin now tells you when the daemon cannot write its own database — a read-only DB (classically a root-owned unmask.sqlite left behind by running unmask migrate as root) keeps serving challenges while silently recording nothing; the retention tab runs an in-daemon write probe with a copy-pasteable fix, and unmask doctor gains the matching check. Per-site challenge logos now actually work (each scope gets its own file instead of overwriting a shared one), and the test pages gain a site picker so a multi-site install can exercise a specific site's challenge end-to-end. Uploaded logos and the setup-wizard token move from /etc/unmask to /var/lib/unmask where variable data belongs.

Settings-save fixes and clearer crawler-spoof visibility. Saving a settings tab no longer silently rewrites values you did not touch — a family of long-standing save bugs is fixed, including the one that pinned the UA black-list's challenge chain onto every challenge (that default action now fires only on an actual black-list match, in both deploy modes). The UA-filter checkbox and the Bypass-IP range presets become independent axes with a live 4-state badge showing each range-backed crawler's true rescue path, so one tab can no longer silently change the other's behavior. The stale-browser tier learns Firefox (ESR stays exempt) and its current-major baselines now auto-follow a daily unmask.sh feed, so the tier keeps tracking new browser releases without manual bookkeeping. The AI-crawler drill-down marks IP-range-verified crawlers with a shield and renames served to challenge — for those vendors the challenged count is spoofed traffic, not the real bot being blocked. Bot hunt gains a User-Agent search and one-click raw-log filters from the rankings. Admin pages now send no-store, so a redeployed dashboard shows its changes on a normal reload.

Security and performance. A spoofed crawler User-Agent no longer walks through the challenge: for vendors that publish official IP ranges (Google, Bing, DuckDuckGo, OpenAI, Perplexity, and now Apple and Amazon), the rescue rides the verified IP ranges instead of the forgeable UA string, so a fake Googlebot from outside Google's ranges is now challenged. A new opt-in stale-browser tier escalates a browser pinned to an outdated Chrome version to a CAPTCHA — the tell of a headless PoW-solving scraper that a real old browser can still clear. Adds four official IP-range presets (Applebot, Amazonbot, DuckAssistBot, Perplexity-User) and lets stats-exclude entries carry a title. The admin dashboard — stats, the landing overview, and settings — is dramatically faster on large multi-site installs: the 30-day charts and the funnel now read background-maintained hourly rollups instead of scanning the full per-site history, so a stats page that took six to eight seconds returns in about two.

Critical fix for a connection leak introduced by 0.1.5's compose mode. On nginx 1.17.6+, every composed challenge or rate-limit redirect left its client connection permanently orphaned; the orphans accumulated until nginx ran out of worker connections and stopped answering entirely — on a busy protected site, within hours. The fix pairs the module's internal redirect with the request-reference release nginx expects (the X-Accel-Redirect idiom). If you run 0.1.5 with nginx 1.17.6 or newer, upgrade now and restart nginx — a reload does not replace the loaded module, and only a restart releases connections already orphaned.

Two over-blocking bugs and a scale fix. A daemon restart used to silently rewrite every inherit-action ban as a hard block, so a honeypot ban configured as a recoverable challenge became an unappealable 403 on every upgrade or reboot; and a honeypot probe arriving on the plaintext port could earn an auto-ban covering the scanner's whole IP. Both are fixed. The stats and bot-hunt pages no longer slow down as stored events accumulate (a new `unmask db-analyze` builds the query-planner statistics SQLite never had), the admin dashboard no longer redirect-loops when a long session outlives its CSRF cookie, and the nginx module stops flooding error.log with uninitialized-variable warnings. The rate-limit/challenge composition is now selected by the host nginx version (1.17.6+) rather than deny-zone presence. Adds a dashboard card showing what the Community Bans feed actually stopped.

Admin-settings polish and a health-check safety net: unmask doctor now probes :80 as a load-balancer health checker and warns if a redirect would drop the node, the network tab's custom IP / host lists become structured add/delete rows instead of newline textareas (with a default-off private-networks preset for stats-exclude), the HTTPS-redirect exemptions adopt the preset/custom two-badge layout, you can delete the last row of any custom list, and the hunt log's clipped 'already BANned' pill is fixed and localized.

Theme-tab preview fixes and a preview-language selector: the preview no longer redirects to the site for operators who already hold a pass cookie, an 18-locale language dropdown lets you preview any language, the over-block banner renders its dash correctly, and unmask doctor warns when https_redirect is enabled but not yet rendered.

HTTP→HTTPS redirect option (off by default, LB-aware, ACME-exempt); bypass-path presets gain per-preset factory defaults (machine-access presets ON out of the box); access-log parser no longer drops the trip URL / UA on TLS-resumption lines; events-table tooltip dedup and sites-tab wording fixes.

Install-path fixes found by dogfooding: postinstall now always restarts onto the new binary (upgrade/reinstall admin-loop fix); protect.inc exempts the /unmask/ machinery when included at server scope; libcrypto detection falls back to nginx -V when ldd is silent (static OpenSSL builds); unmask doctor warns on server-scope protect.inc.
